Expected source behavior: Epoch- or CCD-dependent disappearance; may coincide with defect map
Evidence that strengthens it: Feature repeats in detector coordinates; correlated with image masks, PSF or scattered light
Observation that would weaken it: Independent facilities detect same disappearance at same time while target is on differing detectors
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Can imitate achromatic rapid steps and angularly correlated noise
Critical measurements: Raw cutouts; detector ID; flags; PSF; background; repeat visits
Likely waveband behavior: Any; may look grey or filter-dependent
Duration / cadence considerations: Often single visit or epoch dependent

Expected source behavior: Historical source lacks present catalog counterpart despite actual source presence
Evidence that strengthens it: Propagating proper motion and PSF positional likelihood restores identity
Observation that would weaken it: Distinct repeatably located source remains absent in independent images despite adequate depth
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Nearby blends, historical plate defects, color/filter mismatches
Critical measurements: Gaia proper motions; image cutouts; source association posterior
Duration / cadence considerations: Multi-year to decade catalog baseline; no true flux event
Highest-priority experiment: Motion-aware multi-catalog matching and human image audit

Expected source behavior: Apparent fading or nondetection in dense scenes
Evidence that strengthens it: Flux instability follows PSF seeing and deblending; forced phot restores
Observation that would weaken it: Isolated reproducible source with consistent independent high-resolution light curve
Critical measurements: Deblend model; crowd density; seeing; neighbor flux
Highest-priority experiment: Inject stars into crowded pixels and retest

Expected source behavior: Recurring intrinsic brightness and often color/temperature changes
Evidence that strengthens it: Stable period or quasi-period tied to stellar class and spectra
Observation that would weaken it: Strong foreground extinction tracer / synchronized adjacent-source dip
Critical measurements: Dense multiband light curve; color/spectra; recurrence
Highest-priority experiment: Fit class-informed stochastic and periodic models

Expected source behavior: Repeated geometric dips with orbital recurrence
Evidence that strengthens it: Repeatable timings, phase-folded duration, radial-velocity/astrometric support
Observation that would weaken it: Irregular unrelated nonperiodic dips across stars with foreground alignment
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Circumstellar rings, stellar spots, missed periods
Critical measurements: Timing; eclipse morphology; radial velocities; high cadence
Likely waveband behavior: May be approximately grey; chromatic limb darkening
Duration / cadence considerations: Hours to months; recurrence may exceed baseline
Highest-priority experiment: Search recurrence and follow-up radial velocity

Hypothesis / mechanism: Circumstellar / circumsecondary disk or dusty ring occultation
Evidence level: Observed in selected cases; model-dependent details
Expected source behavior: Deep, structured, potentially flat-bottomed long dimming
Evidence that strengthens it: Ingress substructure, IR excess, co-moving gas lines, repeatability if orbital
Observation that would weaken it: No associated dust/companion signs despite high-quality diagnostics
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Opaque foreground cloud; intrinsic disk/accretion changes
Critical measurements: Optical+IR SED; H-alpha; polarimetry; resolved imaging
Likely waveband behavior: Usually reddening or IR excess; thick occulters may look grey
Duration / cadence considerations: Weeks to years; long orbital recurrence
Highest-priority experiment: Cross-match infrared excess and ingress shape

Expected source behavior: Dimming correlated with wavelength-dependent optical depth
Evidence that strengthens it: Reddening/polarization/gas tracer spatial alignment; dust-compliant extinction fit
Observation that would weaken it: Repeated strictly grey dips with no evidence of grains despite high sensitivity
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Grey dust, opaque clouds, intrinsic reddening, atmospheric extinction
Critical measurements: Calibrated optical/near-IR colors; dust map; polarimetry; CO/HI
Population / sky covariate: Galactic latitude, dust column, molecular regions
Likely waveband behavior: Usually chromatic; variable curve, not universal lambda^-1
Duration / cadence considerations: Cloud chord time from angular size and transverse speed
Highest-priority experiment: Model cloud populations and cross-star correlated extinction

Expected source behavior: Fast extinction/step of stellar flux, potential diffraction
Evidence that strengthens it: Event timed with ephemeris; multi-site moving shadow; Fresnel signature
Observation that would weaken it: No plausible body trajectory at required sensitivity and geometry
Critical measurements: High-cadence multi-site images; occultation geometry; ephemerides
Likely waveband behavior: Often approximately achromatic in broadband geometric limit
Duration / cadence considerations: Milliseconds to minutes often; larger bodies longer

Expected source behavior: Rare unresolved obscuration with finite-source ingress
Evidence that strengthens it: Repeatable multiband extinction edge; astrometric/IR companion evidence
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Dust filament, Solar System occulter, brown-dwarf disk
Critical measurements: Event duration; proper motions; IR imaging; astrometry
Highest-priority experiment: Injection recovery over simulated size and velocity functions

Expected source behavior: Symmetric magnification, generally not isolated-star demagnification
Evidence that strengthens it: Achromatic brightening; astrometric shift; fit t_E and blending
Observation that would weaken it: Flux drop below unlensed baseline attributed solely to isolated positive point lens
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Variable source; blending; other lens configurations
Likely waveband behavior: Geometric optics nearly achromatic; blends introduce chromaticity
Duration / cadence considerations: Days to months typical, broad distribution
Highest-priority experiment: Fit standard finite-source lens and source-blend model

Expected source behavior: Extra image pairs appear/disappear; total source flux can cross detection limit
Evidence that strengthens it: Finite-source fold/cusp morphology with neighboring macroimages and foreground massive lens
Observation that would weaken it: No strong-lensing geometry; source stays bright in independent full-image photometry
Critical measurements: Resolved images; lens mass model; multiband photometry
Duration / cadence considerations: Microlens and source relative proper motion
Highest-priority experiment: Image-plane total-flux modeling incl finite-source caustics

Evidence level: Established weak-lensing effect; rapid wink unproven
Expected source behavior: Modest, usually slowly varying dimming relative to smooth-universe reference
Evidence that strengthens it: Correlated shear/convergence and foreground void maps, consistent distance scaling
Observation that would weaken it: Strong short-lived total blackout without viable curvature/time variation
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Dust, magnification bias, source intrinsic variability
Critical measurements: Weak shear maps; distances; galaxy-density maps; light curves
Duration / cadence considerations: Usually long evolution; short wink implausible without additional dynamics
Highest-priority experiment: Compare residual brightness with preregistered void map

Evidence level: Established at radio; optical efficacy not established
Expected source behavior: Frequency-dependent flux minima/caustics with wandering images
Evidence that strengthens it: Radio dynamic-spectrum frequency scaling; scattering/dispersion changes
Observation that would weaken it: Strict optical effect predicted despite implausibly weak electron refraction and radio nondetection
Critical measurements: Radio multi-frequency light curves; dispersion; scintillation; astrometry
Likely waveband behavior: Strong radio chromaticity; optical much weaker
Duration / cadence considerations: Days to months in known radio events
Highest-priority experiment: Radio-optical contemporaneous control and plasma lens transfer

Expected source behavior: Complex chromatic plus astrometric changes / multiple features
Evidence that strengthens it: Joint lens/dust/plasma fits beat single-mechanism controls, physically plausible parameters
Observation that would weaken it: Joint model requires nonphysical column densities or lens masses
Critical measurements: Time-resolved spectrum; images; astrometric centroid; tracer maps
Highest-priority experiment: Joint model comparison with complexity penalties

Hypothesis / mechanism: Permanent stellar end state / failed supernova
Evidence level: Established possible class, but event rarity constrained
Expected source behavior: One-way source disappearance, often not recovery; possible neutrino/dust/spectroscopic remnant
Evidence that strengthens it: Persistent nondetection in deep repeated multi-band observations and evolutionary progenitor prior
Observation that would weaken it: Original source recovered stably; object was transient contaminant
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Outbursts obscured by dust, crossmatch errors
Critical measurements: Decade images; spectra; IR; progenitor mass
Population / sky covariate: Massive evolved stars and star-forming galaxies
Duration / cadence considerations: Years to decades; one-way rather than closed wink
Highest-priority experiment: Independent deep repeat imaging, late-time infrared

Expected source behavior: Sky-coherent, reproducible residual not explained by calibrated known processes
Evidence that strengthens it: Predefined amplitude/timescale distribution reproduces held-out sky-time covariance and flux statistics
Observation that would weaken it: No residual after forward-modeling known matter/instrument effects
Critical measurements: Independent instrument flux/astrometric multi-band + foreground tomography
Population / sky covariate: Specified before holdout, not fit after selection
Likely waveband behavior: Unspecified until derived; achromaticity not identifying
Highest-priority experiment: Independent blind validation with theory-frozen transport law

Evidence level: Exploratory, no validated transfer or event-rate law
Expected source behavior: Only signature derived from explicit model metric/null transport would count
Evidence that strengthens it: Independent geometric derivation predicts quantitative rates/sky covariance before withheld test and passes instrumental/known-lens controls
Observation that would weaken it: Fails preregistered rate/geometry prediction; no unique result beyond conventional models
Major confounder / non-unique clue: Known inhomogeneous GR; obscuration; camera drifts; look-elsewhere effects
Critical measurements: Test only model-locked prediction with complete flux/magnification and selection
Population / sky covariate: No presupposed toroidal stripe or 0.246 rad conversion
Likely waveband behavior: No warranted universal 80% or achromatic prediction
Duration / cadence considerations: Period/rate must be computed, not chosen
Highest-priority experiment: Withhold data until derivation; joint fit with conventional controls
